title: Comal County seeks Attorney General guidance on releasing Bulverde shooting details
text:

School officials and Comal County authorities are still protecting the shooter's identity. The County is turning to the attorney general for guidance.COMAL COUNTY, TX - There are new developments in the push for answers about the 15-year-old shooter who injured a teacher at a Bulverde high school last month.
School officials and Comal County authorities are still protecting the shooter's identity. Now, the county's district attorney is seeking guidance from the Attorney General's office on what they have to share. School officials and Comal County authorities are still protecting the shooter's identity. The County is turning to the attorney general for guidance. We've spent weeks asking Comal County authorities about the identity of shooter at Hill Country College Preparatory High School. The 15-year-old shot a teacher before taking his own life. County officials are still not naming the suspect or victim; we finally received a response. "I know that silence can feel like secrecy," said Comal ISD Superintendent Dr. John E. Chapman III in a video"Privacy protection for students at the elementary and secondary do not expire upon the death of a minor," he said. "Those rights rest with the students' parents. We are bound by that law."Several sources have pointed us to an address believed to be associated with the gunman. On April 7, we submitted an open records request to the Comal County Sheriff's Office — asking for calls for service to that address within the past six years; we didn't specify a reason why. Tonight, we received the county's nearly seven-page briefing to the Texas Attorney General asking for guidance. Not only did that briefing connect the address to the shooting, its Assistant District Attorney also explained the offices' reasoning for not releasing the records. The ADA saying those documents "relate to a critical incident that occurred less than 30 days ago" adding releasing the information "interferes with the on-going investigation." The briefing also points to privacy laws, acknowledging that while adults' privacy rights lapse at death -- under the Texas family code, that concept doesn't apply to the 15-year-old shooter. The briefing mentions the county's "desire for transparency" under the state's public information act while also staying within bounds of the law.We're still working to gather information to bring you answers to the many questions surrounding this shooting, including the gunman's identity. Authorities also have not shared the name of the teacher who was shot.
